definitions.explanation: The weekend of the current week — normally the Saturday and Sunday just ahead, and sometimes Friday evening as well. Used adverbially without a particle as often as it is used as a plain noun.

examples.japanese: {今週末|こんしゅうまつ}は{暇|ひま}です。
{今週末|こんしゅうまつ}、{映画|えいが}を{見|み}に{行|い}きませんか。
examples.english: Would you like to go see a movie this weekend?

examples.japanese: {今週末|こんしゅうまつ}の{予定|よてい}がまだ{決|き}まっていないので、{明日|あした}{連絡|れんらく}します。
examples.english: My plans for this weekend aren't settled yet, so I'll get in touch tomorrow.

notes:
Formed from {今|こん} (this) + {週末|しゅうまつ} (weekend). Like other time words of this shape, it takes no particle when used adverbially: {今週末|こんしゅうまつ}{行|い}きます, not ×{今週末|こんしゅうまつ}に{行|い}きます.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {今週末|こんしゅうまつ}の{予定|よてい}: plans for this weekend
- {今週末|こんしゅうまつ}まで: by this weekend
- {今週末|こんしゅうまつ}は{空|あ}いています: I'm free this weekend

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {来週末|らいしゅうまつ}: next weekend
- {先週末|せんしゅうまつ}: last weekend
- {週末|しゅうまつ}: weekend — no anchoring to a particular week
